Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray and CT images show a reticulonodular pattern that is more prominent in the upper and mid lung zones, with relative sparing of the costophrenic angles (though there is some basal involvement on CT). This upper-lobe predominance is characteristic of Pulmonary Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH), which can also present with pleural effusions.
